answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn fees. A lagoon of idle accounts then ties up capital without gaining influence; splitting one operator across many identities does not multiply the locked stake, while buying enough tokens raises the attacker’s cost and risks slashing for provable fraud. At dawn, honest agents can still join by staking, and a nebula of cheap, unbacked identities has no weight in allocation.
